chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And whoever intends therein by deviation or by injustice We will make him taste of a painful punishment.' He said: 'Every injustice in it is deviation, so if you hit your servant unjustly, I fear it would be deviation; therefore, the jurists dislike residing in Mecca.'

key_terms.إِلْحَاد: Deviation or injustice (specifically in the context of the verse)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'ilhad' in the context of Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the concept of 'ilhad' in the sacred precincts of Mecca to encompass any injustice, even minor acts like striking a servant, thereby elevating the spiritual stakes of daily conduct. This broad interpretation explains the juristic preference against permanent residence in Mecca, as the sanctity of the area demands a higher degree of justice and freedom from transgression than ordinary locales. The hadith thus links the metaphysical severity of 'ilhad' with practical legal rulings regarding habitation and social interactions within the holy city.
